analysis: This unit is test-only: the diff adds four tests to SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift (head lines ~3140-3239) for SSDWholeRootMaintainer header-verdict caching. No production code is visible in this batch, so no security control is changed here. The tests assert behavior relevant to T-041 (at-rest SSD prefix cache, DBK3 ownership proof, TTL/LRU sweeping). (1) remembersHeaderVerdictsOnlyForUnchangedFiles: a header overwritten with the mtime restored must lose its cached ownership verdict. This implies the production cache keys on ctime or inode/identity, not only size+mtime. (2) replacedLookalikeIsReadAgain: a malformed lookalike later replaced by a real block is re-read and becomes owned. (3) failedHeaderReadIsRetried: a transient header-read failure (EACCES here) is not cached as 'not ours' or 'owned', so the file is neither deleted nor permanently skipped. (4) Existing tests (malformedLookalikePreserved, symlinkedRootIsNeverTraversed) keep the fail-safe of never deleting files without DBK3 proof and never traversing symlinked ancestors. These tests tighten confidence in the cleanup path and do not weaken it. Remaining integration questions for the next pass: confirm the production verdict cache in SSDWholeRootMaintainer actually uses ctime plus dev/inode (the test mutates only content and mtime), that failed reads are never memoized, and that the cache is bounded in memory and invalidated per root. The test temp-dir permission toggling (0o100) is restored in defers and is test-local. The rest of the head text (donation gate, write-behind queue bounds, outcome recorder, sidecar tests) is unchanged context, with no visible security regression.
